title: Congressional District Context: Verify First
description: Build the context for finding a congressional district — address and county first — with Congressional District Context, then confirm officially. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, an address near a district line resolves its state and county here first, so the official district lookup that follows starts from verified ground.
quick_answer: Congressional District Context helps you assemble the verified context — the address's state and county — that a congressional district answer stands on, then points you to the authoritative government lookup to confirm the district itself. Locate the address, note its context, and confirm the district on the official source.

Districts are redrawn after each census; yesterday's district can be wrong today. Context tools plus the current official map is the only safe method.
“The district containing…” is a claim to verify, not to vibe. Build the context, confirm on the official tool, cite both steps.

examples.label: Example · The county is not the district

body.t: Large urban counties contain several districts; small rural districts contain several counties. Neither contains the other — which is why context precedes confirmation.
District lines split cities and occasionally streets. Two neighbours can vote in different districts; only the official lookup at the exact address settles it.

faq: Is this the official map?
No — deliberately. This page builds verified context and directs you to the authoritative government lookup for the district itself, because that answer should come from the source of record.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — you supply the address under study; your own location is not involved.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
District maps are redrawn and republishing lags vary. The official current-cycle map is the referee.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
Why not just show the district here?
Because a stale or unofficial district answer is worse than a handoff. Context here is verified; the district itself deserves the official word.
My district changed since last election.
Redistricting after the 2020 census redrew many maps. Current-cycle confirmation is the fix, and this workflow builds it in.
Senate districts or state legislature?
Different maps again — state sources rule those. The context-first method transfers; the official destination changes.
Where is the official lookup?
The US House of Representatives' find-your-representative service, by ZIP and address — the page's workflow ends there deliberately.
ZIP code alone enough for the official step?
ZIPs cross district lines; the official tool asks for the full address when a ZIP straddles. Your context from this page explains why.
State legislative districts too?
Your state legislature's site holds those maps. The context-first method is identical.
